title: Get Warned Before a DHCP Scope Runs Out of Addresses

cta.text: See Micetro with your Microsoft DHCP servers

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Get Warned Before a DHCP Scope Runs Out of Addresses".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Get an Email Before a DHCP Scope Runs Dry" and whose text is exactly: See how BlueCat Micetro watches a Windows DHCP scope and emails your team when its free addresses drop below a limit you choose.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
7 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. This guest Wi-Fi scope on a Windows DHCP server has plenty of free addresses today, and nobody is watching it. Next you will tell Micetro to. Open the scope's row menu.
2. Monitoring is a setting on the subnet itself. Choose Set subnet monitoring.
3. Turn it on, give it an address to tell, and say how few free addresses is too few: ten, here. One message is enough until the problem is fixed. Select Save.
4. Subnet monitoring now reads Yes. Micetro watches this scope's free addresses for you. Now a rush of new devices arrives and takes 21 of the 30 addresses.
5. The scope is 70% used and nine addresses are left, below the limit of ten. Micetro should already be telling the team. Check the team's inbox.
6. Micetro emailed the team before any client failed to get an address. Open the message.
7. It names the subnet, how many addresses are left and the threshold, so whoever reads it knows exactly what to fix.
